finding: Truth coercion of a long UTF-16 carrier previously performed a full decode and lossy UTF-8 conversion while charging one step; a 4096-unit input with max_steps=64 returned complete success.
change: Borrow tagged UTF-16 carrier and perform an exact lossy UTF-8 length pass plus output pass; both charge UTF-16 units and cancellation. Reserve exactly the logical output bytes through SQLite ToSql; empty output takes no reservation. Native UTF-8 input precharges byte validation and counts output units. Invalid carriers remain errors and bytes/numeric follow their separate paths.

red.observation: NativeV1 SELECT 1 WHERE long text succeeded with only 64 SQL steps; test stopped at first case.

intermediate.exact-workspace: One test failed when 10000 was assumed sufficient but 14096 was observed; 4096 is another concurrent logical reservation of unproven origin.
intermediate.empty-red: One test failed when a zero-byte output attempted the 10001st live reservation.
intermediate.surrogate-boundary: Test compilation failed because unwrap_err required Reservation: Debug; corrected test and retained.

limits: Synthetic bridge and session checks; not actual HostLab/A0/A1 or full SQL qualification. UTF-8 validation is a synchronous precharged scan and is not hard-interruptible. UTF-16 exact-size prepass and output pass both charge work and add processing; no performance measurement. In the tested query 14095 bytes failed and 14096 succeeded because 4096 other logical bytes coexisted; their precise origin was not measured. Input/provider/SQLite buffers, other carrier decoding, allocator overhead and RSS are outside this proof. SQLite truth is checked on explicitly lossy display, not raw MUTF-8 identity.
